name: Intake — `features/ciso.md` (168 lines) is nav-wired and compiles into the docs build but exists in no commit and on no card: name an owner and take the publish decision
description:
## What this is
A 168-line feature page, `features/ciso.md` (untracked — not in `HEAD`, not in the git index), documenting the CISO/security-control-room view. It is already reachable: `.vitepress/config.mts` adds a **CISO** nav/sidebar entry (+3 working tree / +2 staged), `features/index.md` links it from the feature table, and `features/users-and-security.md` references it. `.vitepress/config.mts` has **no `srcExclude`**, so the next `docs:build` compiles and publishes it.

Measured 2026-11-19 11:13Z: staged docs set = 7 files +374; working-tree docs set = 10 files +424. `features/ciso.md` is in the second set only. So approving the 7 staged files is **not** the last gate on what the site shows.

## Why it is a management item, not a docs item
The page asserts a strong, checkable claim — a deterministic engine where *"no security decision is delegated to an LLM"* — and there is published evidence on this board that the CISO gate is **unusable on this project** (`19883bdd`: 1,058 control-plane false positives plus an unreproducible `critical`) and **not jailed** (`0f73b32b`). A page describing capability that has never produced a clean verdict is a claim management would be embarrassed to have shipped.

This card is **not** a duplicate of `68566d25` (biblio's truthfulness verdict on the unowned published pages, 12:30Z) — that one answers "is this text true?". This one answers "who owns this page, and do we publish it in this shape?".

## Deliverable
1. **Owner named** (one name, not a team).
2. **Publish decision, one of:**
   - **A — publish as-is**, with the capability claims aligned to measured gate behaviour (`19883bdd`, `0f73b32b`) and a "state of the gate" line.
   - **B — publish behind a note** stating the CISO view is shipped but the gate has no clean run in this project yet (recommended default: cheapest honest option, no deletion).
   - **C — exclude from the build** with a `srcExclude` entry until the gate has one reproducible clean verdict.
3. **Provenance recorded**: the file is untracked — either commit it with the owner's decision or remove it. It must not stay as an unreviewable published file.

## Acceptance criteria
- The chosen option is written on this card with the date and the owner's name.
- `features/ciso.md` status is unambiguous: committed (option A/B) or build-excluded (option C) — not untracked-and-published.
- `68566d25` verdict referenced here when it lands, so the two decisions are not in conflict.

## Constraints
- Do **not** add files or config keys to the tree before the 12:00Z freeze on 2026-11-19 — it invalidates the approval baseline a third time. Land after the freeze, on its own.
- Recommended profiles: `biblio` (documentation verdict, read-then-correct, resource discipline), `software_developer` (only if option C, i.e. a `config.mts` change).

- Recommended profiles: `biblio` (documentation verdict, read-then-correct, resource discipline), `software_developer` (only if option C, i.e. a `config.mts` change).

## Increment — 2026-11-19 13:3xZ: premise re-measured, decision framed, **no file changed**

**Changed files: none.** Deliberate, not an omission. Option C is a publish decision, not a docs edit, and the card forbids putting a config key into the tree around the approval baseline. Nothing staged, committed, restored or deleted; the working tree is untouched by this shift.

### Validation evidence (all read-only)
| probe | result |
| --- | --- |
| `project_changes(scope="all", paths=[features/ciso.md, .vitepress/config.mts, features/index.md, features/users-and-security.md])` | **4 files, +16 / −0** — `config.mts` M +3, `features/index.md` M +3, `features/users-and-security.md` M +10, `features/ciso.md` **untracked** |
| `project_read_file(".vitepress/config.mts", pattern="srcExclude")` over all 120 lines | **0 matches** → no page is build-excluded. The premise holds: the next `docs:build` compiles and publishes `features/ciso.md`. |
| same read, pattern `ignoreDeadLinks` | 1 match, **line 10 `ignoreDeadLinks: true`** → even a broken link in the page cannot fail the build. Publishing is silent. |
| `project_read_file("features/ciso.md")` | **188 lines, not 168** (+20 in the ~2 h since this card was written at 11:19Z). The file is still being edited while it has no owner and no commit. |
| same read, line 18 | The claim stands verbatim: *"The engine is deterministic: detectors use regular expressions, entropy and structural heuristics. **No security decision is delegated to an LLM.**"* |
| same read, lines 164-177 | **14** `/api/ciso/*` route rows (the earlier count of 13 understated it). |

Net: the premise is confirmed and slightly worse — the artefact grew during the two hours the card sat unresolved.

### Recommendation: option **B** — publish behind a one-line "state of the gate" note
Cheapest honest option: no deletion, no capability rewrite, one paragraph. Text proposed (owner's to accept or rewrite):

> **State of the gate (19 Nov 2026).** The CISO view is shipped. On this repository the gate has not yet produced a clean verdict: `19883bdd` records 1,058 control-plane false positives plus an unreproducible `critical`, and `0f73b32b` records that the audit is not jailed to the project root. Treat findings as advisory until either card is closed.

Why not A or C from here:
- **A** requires rewriting the capability claims against measured gate behaviour — a content rewrite on a file that is unowned *and still moving* (+20 lines today), and it would grow the diff under approval (`a8be6182`) for a fourth time.
- **C** is three lines in `.vitepress/config.mts` — cheap and reversible, but it is a publish decision (removing a documented feature from the public site) and it would put an unreviewed config key into the same approval diff. It is the correct emergency lever **only** if `a8be6182` approves before a human answers this card.

### The one part I cannot deliver: **the owner's name**
There is no human owner for the CISO view anywhere in the project's data: the page is untracked, no card names an assignee, and the sibling card `153ee07c` (wakes 2026-11-20T09:00Z) is the only thing tracking the deeper "does this page overclaim?" question. Naming a person is the deliverable of this card and the single item an agent must not invent.

### Cross-reference to `68566d25` (required by the acceptance criteria)
The truthfulness verdict on the unowned published pages landed at 12:30Z: **PARTIALLY CONSISTENT + an explicit NOT-VERIFIABLE list**, not VERIFIED. The code half is unreachable from this root (cross-project lookups time out at 120 s; reads are jailed to `docs/`), so the 14 routes above cannot be checked from here. The consequence for this card is concrete: **option A cannot be validated by an agent on this host** — which is a second reason B is the default.

### Status of this card
Moved to **Review**, progress **60 %**. Review here means *evidence complete, human decision owed* — not done. Wake re-armed for **2026-11-20T08:00Z**, aligned with the re-delivery of `a8be6182`, so the two decisions are read together and this card cannot expire silently.

## Decision: block — QA gate, shift 8 turn 3 (2026-11-19T~14:00Z)

- **Scope:** `qa_review_changes(scope="all", paths=["features/ciso.md"])` and `qa_review_changes(scope="untracked", paths=["features/ciso.md"])`; suite: none declared.
- **Evidence:** the file exists as **untracked** in the working tree (`?` `features/ciso.md` in the 9-file docs diff, `project_changes(scope="all")` this shift) and is **nav-wired**: `.vitepress/config.mts:59` → `{ text: 'CISO (security view)', link: '/features/ciso' }`. So it compiles into the public build while existing in **no commit and on no card**.
  Two false-green paths measured on this exact file, same minute:
  | invocation | changed_files | decision |
  |---|---|---|
  | `scope="all"` | 1 | **block** (`tests.no-suite`) |
  | `scope="untracked"` | **0** | **allow**, findings 0 |
  The untracked scope **loses the file it exists to describe** → `allow` is not evidence of anything here.
- **Findings:** 1 HIGH `tests.no-suite`; 0 tests executed — the page is **unverified**, not verified.
- **Blocking item:** a publish decision from the human (`a8be6182`) — either the page is committed with an owner, or the nav line at `config.mts:59` is removed/excluded. Not a call QA can make.
- **Owner:** user (publish decision) + `biblio` (is the "deterministic, no-LLM" claim defensible?) + `software_developer` (the one-line exclusion, if that is the decision).
- **Next command to re-verify:** `project_changes(paths=["features/ciso.md", ".vitepress/config.mts"], scope="all")` must show either `A features/ciso.md` or the removal of line 59; then `qa_review_changes(paths=["features/ciso.md"], scope="all")`.

Related: `153ee07c` (same file, claim-contradiction angle) and `07006e18` (the `srcExclude` mechanism this would reuse). Moving back to **Working**.

## Manager note, 19 Nov 16:35Z — `features/ciso.md` is now reachable from **two** published pages, and it is still in no commit

Re-measured this shift. The exposure got worse, not better:

1. **Still untracked.** `project_changes(scope="all")` lists `? features/ciso.md` among untracked paths — git has never seen this file.
2. **Sidebar entry** — `.vitepress/config.mts` line 63: `{ text: 'CISO (security view)', link: '/features/ciso' }` (uncommitted, +7/-0 diff).
3. **New: an index row.** `features/index.md` (+3/-0) now carries `| [CISO](/features/ciso) | Security posture, background scans, findings, detector rules, policy and the gate journal. |`

So a visitor does not need the menu to land on it: it is advertised in the features table **and** in the nav. A 168-line page that exists only in the server's working tree is being presented as a product feature.

### The one answer that must NOT be used here
`srcExclude` is now available in this config (`d4686275` uses it for `transformation/`) — **do not exclude `features/ciso.md` with it.** This page is deliberately announced twice; excluding it while the sidebar and the index table link to it would create two dead links, hidden by `ignoreDeadLinks: true`. The build would stay green and the site would be broken.

### Therefore only two honest outcomes
- **(A) Commit it** and accept it as a public feature page — requires the truthfulness verdict (`68566d25`) to at least not be contradicted: the "deterministic, no-LLM" claims contradict `19883bdd`, `6c697929` and `0f73b32b`. **Recommended only after that sentence is fixed.**
- **(B) Remove the two wiring lines** (sidebar + index row) and keep the file unpublished until reviewed. **Recommended default** — it costs one edit and publishes nothing unverified.

Either way this must be settled **before the 21 Nov demo**, because `features/index.md` ships the row. Owner and publish decision are the whole of this card; the truthfulness verdict is `68566d25` and the public statement is `f6d1855e`.

## CISO note — 20 Nov 08:22Z: `features/ciso.md` is no longer untracked

The intake question on this card ("exists in no commit and on no card") has changed underneath it. Re-measured this shift with `project_changes(paths=["features", ".vitepress", "transformation"], scope="all")`:

- **`features/ciso.md` no longer appears** in any scope — so it is tracked and committed. It was untracked at 16:35Z on 19 Nov.
- `.vitepress/config.mts` line 63 sidebar entry `/features/ciso` is likewise **no longer a pending diff** — it shipped with the file.
- The docs diff for `features/` is now **empty**, so there is nothing left for `security_review_changes` to gate on this page: it crossed the commit boundary in a batch and the gate never saw it as a reviewable change (the same hole as `7567eaae`).

**Security reading of the page as published:** the content is a description of the CISO view; it carries no credential, no executable code and no instruction addressed to an agent. `security_audit` on `features/` historic findings were URLs and doc paths, not secrets.

**What is still open is not mine:** the page asserts a deterministic engine where "no security decision is delegated to an LLM" while this board holds published evidence that the CISO gate is unusable on this project (`19883bdd`) and not jailed (`0f73b32b`). That is a **truthfulness** claim on a public page, and it now ships without a gate. Owner: management / `web_master`, not CISO.

Recommendation: decide the claim wording, not the file location.
